chapter_seo_title: Dao-Twisted Chapter 240: Fengdu's Two-Headed Daoist and the Heart-Element Reveal
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang finally reaches the Fengdu exit. But his guide, Han Fu, has a secret body part—and he's known about Li Huowang's Heart-Element all along. A perfect slow-burn horror reveal chapter.
og_description: Han Fu peels off Li Huowang's mask and grins with both mouths. The Heart-Element is exposed, and the darkness is now a hunting ground.
twitter_description: Han Fu the Daoist has two heads and zero trust. His reveal turns a friendly conversation into a deadly chase—and confirms a terrifying truth about the Heavenly Calamity cycle.

lore_anchors.definition: The Chinese underworld city; in this novel, it is a nesting network of dark caves beneath Qingqiu.
A folk-horror entity in the Dao-Twisted World that is fed old people in exchange for their estates; its name sounds playful, but its practice is brutal.
An ontological disaster where a fundamental law of reality (e.g., rot, lies) ceases to function; a recurring, systemic event tied to the Dao of the Siming.
A rare human constitution that makes the bearer a powerful alchemical ingredient; its exposure makes Li Huowang a target for anyone who can claim him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Han Fu knock off Li Huowang's mask?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He wanted to confirm his suspicion that Li Huowang was a Heart-Element before revealing his true nature and attempting to trap him in Fengdu.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What was the “Little Girl” voice from the darkness?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It was Han Fu’s second, infantile head speaking; he was never arguing with a separate entity, just performing a one-man show to keep Li Huowang guessing.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does the “disappearance of Lies” mean for the world?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Every Heavenly Calamity removes one rule from reality; when Lies vanished, even the Zuowandao couldn’t function, confirming these are systemic, cyclical overwrites of existence.
